projects.title: A finalized statement that stays final.
projects.headline: An eight-month billing rewrite, from workflow definition through validation.
projects.context: Customer statements needed to be dependable records of completed billing periods. Finance, customer-facing teams, and customers all relied on the same information.
projects.problem: Later account activity could change a finalized statement. That made it harder to explain a billing period and rely on the statement as a fixed record.
projects.role: I owned the end-to-end business workflow and development of the associated reporting. I partnered with Finance, Product, and Engineering on requirements, implementation, testing, and rollout; engineering delivery was a cross-functional effort.
approach: Documented the existing statement behavior and the business requirements for a finalized record.
Connected the billing workflow and reporting requirements across Finance, Product, and Engineering.
Worked through testing and validation to check the revised behavior against the original problem.
Carried the business workflow through rollout and reporting delivery.
projects.solution: A revised billing workflow and supporting reporting that preserved finalized statements after subsequent account activity.
results: Delivered the billing rewrite over eight months.
Finalized statements remained fixed after finalization.
Customers and internal teams had a dependable record of the completed billing period.
projects.next: Extend regression coverage to statement edge cases and track recurring billing exceptions so new changes preserve the same control.
projects.evidence: The eight-month duration is an actual delivery timeline, not a claimed reduction against a prior schedule.

projects.title: One process from source reports to partner payouts.
projects.headline: Centralized merchant mappings, revenue-share rules, reconciliation, and reporting.
projects.context: Revenue-share operations connect source reports, merchant relationships, partner calculations, and payments. Leadership needs to understand both what the business earns and how the underlying activity supports that result.
projects.problem: Separate files and partner-specific calculations make recurring reporting difficult to follow. A mismatch can originate in source data, merchant mapping, calculation rules, or payment activity; those differences need to remain traceable.
projects.role: I own the end-to-end operational workflow and reporting development, including recurring reconciliation and investigation of revenue-share discrepancies. I coordinate with internal stakeholders to clarify rules and resolve exceptions.
approach: Centralized merchant mappings and partner setup so recurring calculations use consistent reference data.
Brought monthly revenue, revenue-share calculations, partner statements, reconciliation, and payout tracking into a connected workbook.
Built validation and exception views to investigate differences and compare revised outputs with the legacy process.
Developed reporting for different audiences and documented recurring steps to make the process easier to maintain.
projects.solution: A redesigned revenue-share tracker with connected reference data, calculation logic, reconciliation, payout tracking, and partner and management reporting.
results: Centralized the inputs and reporting needed to follow revenue-share activity through the workflow.
Made merchant mapping, partner logic, reconciliation, and payout status available within a connected tracking process.
Created a structure for recurring exception investigation and reporting; the contract work is ongoing.
projects.next: Prioritize repeatable imports and exception checks for automation, while preserving source traceability and approval controls.
projects.evidence: The public samples use fictional entities and illustrative figures. They demonstrate the method and are not employer records or measured business results.

projects.title: Compensation rules translated into calculation logic.
projects.headline: Connected approved plan requirements to CaptivateIQ calculations and validation.
projects.context: A commission process needs to translate approved compensation plans into consistent calculations that Finance and Sales can understand and review.
projects.problem: The manual process was becoming harder to maintain. Moving into a platform required translating plan rules carefully, validating the underlying data, and investigating unexpected outputs.
projects.role: I contributed to the CaptivateIQ implementation by translating compensation requirements, validating source data and outputs, and investigating exceptions. My contribution sat within the broader implementation effort.
approach: Worked from approved compensation requirements to define calculation logic.
Checked source data and calculated outputs for consistency with those requirements.
Investigated exceptions during testing and supported the implementation work.
projects.solution: Calculation logic and validation work supporting the move from a manual commission process into CaptivateIQ.
results: Translated compensation requirements into system calculation logic.
Validated source data and outputs and investigated exceptions during implementation.
Supported the move from manual calculations to a structured commission platform.
projects.next: Maintain a reusable set of test cases covering plan changes, unusual transactions, and payout exceptions.
projects.evidence: No confidential compensation terms, payout amounts, or unverified efficiency metrics are included.
